## Goal

Make "won a game" a first-class, engine-generic achievement event so the give-away triggers have a real, Steam-free source.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `AchievementSystem` (or a documented thin extension) gains an idempotent game-outcome surface (e.g. `onGameOutcome({ gameId, outcome })`) that unlocks mapped achievements via the existing `AchievementSink`; zero Steam/Electron imports.
- The launcher manifest defines `first-win` and `second-distinct-game-win` meta-achievements (titles, descriptions, hidden flags) and the outcome-to-achievement mapping is engine-generic.
- "Second distinct game" logic only unlocks after wins in two different game ids; re-wins of the same game do not.
- `SteamAchievementService` idempotence and offline paths are reused unchanged for the meta-achievements.
- Unit tests cover outcome-to-unlock, distinct-game counting, idempotence, and no-op for unknown outcomes; pass under `--project unit`.

## Key Files

- `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts`
- `src/core-engine/index.ts`
- `electron/achievement-manifest.json`
- `tests/steam-achievements/achievement-outcome.test.ts` (new)

## Deliverables

Engine outcome surface, manifest meta-achievements, unit tests.
data.title: Engine game-outcome surface and cross-game meta-achievements

# Pin the Phaser-free `@ui` node import surface as a machine-checked contract

**Headline:** The `@ui` barrel is Phaser-bearing by design, so downstream game
unit suites must import deep Phaser-free paths. Today that rule lives only in
prose (plus an evaluation-based test guard) and names a handful of modules
incidentally. This item pins the surface explicitly — a typed, machine-readable
manifest of modules guaranteed importable in a Node environment with no
`window` — and enforces it with a static import-graph check that fails when a
listed module transitively reaches a Phaser **value** import, without depending
on test execution order.

## Problem statement

`CG-0MVQQ2M8E003FQMZ` fixed the immediate regression (a Phaser value import
leaking into `illegalMoveToastView` and, through it, `@ui/shakeIllegalMove` and
`@ui/dragDrop`) and added a Node-environment guard
(`tests/ui/phaser-free-imports.test.ts`) that imports each framework-free entry
point under a throwing `phaser` mock. What remains missing is a *contract*:

- There is no canonical, machine-readable statement of **which** `src/ui`
  modules are node-safe. `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
  (§ "Phaser-free `@ui` helper imports for Node tests", ~line 1817) names four
  modules in prose and adds "other `@ui` modules (e.g. `@ui/screen-layout`,
  `@ui/constants`) are also Phaser-free. When in doubt, probe with a readonly
  `vite-node` import" — i.e. the guidance for the common case is *empirical
  probing*, not a lookup.
- The only enforcement is **evaluation-based** (the module actually has to be
  imported inside a Vitest file for the mock to fire). A listed module that is
  never imported by the guard, or a listing added later, is silently unguarded.
  The guard also cannot distinguish "listed module is safe" from "listed module
  is untested".
- The barrel caveat (`@ui` itself is Phaser-bearing because
  `CardGameScene extends Phaser.Scene`) is documented, but only as prose inside
  one developer-guide section; nothing at the barrel's own definition site says
  "never import this from a Node test".

## Users and user stories

- **Downstream game producer/agent:** "As a producer in a `tce-<game>` repo, I
  can look up whether a given `@ui` module is safe to import from a Node unit
  test instead of running an ad-hoc `vite-node` probe and hoping I read the
  crash correctly."
- **Engine maintainer:** "As an engine maintainer, when I add a Phaser value
  import (or a `./Renderer` import) to a module on the node-safe list, a core
  check fails immediately and names the module and the offending import chain —
  not 23 downstream suites with `window is not defined` (`CG-0MVQQ2M8E003FQMZ`)."
- **Engine maintainer growing the surface:** "As an engine maintainer, adding a
  module to the guaranteed surface is one edit to one list, and the check proves
  the new entry actually satisfies the contract before it is promised."
- **Game scene author (unchanged behaviour):** "As a scene author I keep
  importing whatever `@ui` path I like from scene code; nothing about runtime
  behaviour, animation, or the barrel's exports changes."

## Existing state (evidence, verified read-only in this intake)

- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` § *Phaser-free `@ui` helper imports for Node tests*
  (line ~1817) already states the rule, the barrel caveat, the guard file, and
  cross-links this item (`CG-0MVS9HBN3009HIQN`). It is prose only — no list
  exists in code.
- `tests/ui/phaser-free-imports.test.ts` exists and guards exactly four deep
  entry points (`illegalMoveToastView`, `shakeIllegalMove`, `dragDrop`,
  `illegalMoveToast`) with a file-scoped throwing `vi.mock('phaser')` plus a
  negative control (`@ui/Renderer`). Its module docblock already points at this
  item for "the broader documented Phaser-free node surface + static import-graph
  check".
- A read-only regex import-graph probe over `src/ui/*.ts` in this intake found
  **44** modules with no transitive Phaser value import and **18** Phaser-bearing
  ones (`CardGameScene`, `createCardGame`, `GameSelectorScene`, `HelpPanel`,
  `HelpButton`, `SettingsPanel`, `SettingsButton`, `SceneHeader`, `HighlightManager`,
  `HintBar`, `Slider`, `Tooltip`, `hiDpiText`, `versionDisplay`, `AlphaBadge`,
  `CardPackListing`, `GymSceneUtils`, `index`). The probe was **regex-based and
  approximate** (it does not follow `@core-engine/*` / `@card-system/*` /
  `@rule-engine/*` / `@ai/*` / `@ui/*` path aliases, `export * from`, or dynamic
  `import()`), so the real numbers must come from the new compiler-based check.
  That gap is itself evidence for building the check rather than trusting a
  hand-written list.
- Sibling repos exist locally (`../tce-beleaguered-castle`, `../tce-blackjack`,
  `../tce-coloretto`, `../tce-feudalism`, `../tce-golf`,
  `../tce-lost-cities`, `../tce-main-street`, `../tce-sushi-go`,
  `../tce-the-rising`, …). A read-only census of their deep `@ui/...` imports
  shows the framework-free modules they actually reach for are a small,
  identifiable set (`@ui/screen-layout*`, `@ui/constants`, `@ui/SettingsStore`,
  `@ui/dragDrop`, `@ui/shakeIllegalMove`, `@ui/PileView`, `@ui/Overlay`,
  `@ui/game-plugin-boot`, `@ui/card-pack-client`, `@ui/card-pack-url`,
  `@ui/content-unlock-client`, `@ui/CardPackLoader`, `@ui/popTextOrIcon`,
  `@ui/moveGameObject`, `@ui/discardCard`), while the rest of their usage is
  scene-only (`@ui/createCardGame`, `@ui/Renderer*`, `@ui/CardGameScene`,
  `@ui/HelpPanel`, `@ui/Tooltip`, `@ui/debug/*`).
- Tooling precedent for repo checks exists: `scripts/check-terminology-guards.sh`,
  `scripts/check-browser-test-env.ts`, `scripts/check-steamworks.mjs`, plus
  `tests/scripts/*.test.ts` unit coverage for each script. `typescript` (5.9.3)
  is already a dev dependency, so a compiler-API check needs **no new
  dependency**.
- No existing item covers this: `wl search` over *phaser*, *node-safe*,
  *import guard*, *window is not defined*, *ui barrel* returns
  `CG-0MVQQ2M8E003FQMZ` (the fix that **caused** the follow-up and explicitly
  defers option C here) and `CG-0MVPXFHBZ004LGEB` (the toast feature). No
  duplicate; this item is the deferred remainder.

## Desired change

1. **Typed manifest (single source of truth).** Add
   `src/ui/node-safe-modules.ts` exporting a readonly, `as const` list of the
   `src/ui` module paths guaranteed to be importable in a Node environment (no
   `window`, no Phaser evaluation), each with a one-line rationale comment
   (what it is / why it must stay framework-free). The file must itself be
   Phaser-free and side-effect-free (a plain data module) so it can be imported
   by the check, the guard test and docs tooling. Candidate initial entries
   (each to be **verified** by the new check during implementation, not assumed):
   `illegalMoveToast`, `illegalMoveToastView`, `shakeIllegalMove`, `dragDrop`,
   `screen-layout`, `screen-layout-compose`, `screen-layout-schema`,
   `constants`, `SettingsStore`, `card-pack-url`, `card-pack-client`,
   `game-asset-url`, `game-manifest`, `game-plugin-boot`, `content-unlock-client`.
2. **Static import-graph check.** Add `scripts/check-ui-node-surface.ts`
   (TypeScript compiler API — `typescript` is already a devDependency; no new
   package) that, for **every** entry in the manifest:
   - resolves and walks the module graph from that entry using the same
     `paths`/aliases as `tsconfig.json` (so `@core-engine/*`, `@card-system/*`,
     `@rule-engine/*`, `@ai/*`, `@ui/*` are followed, not skipped);
   - ignores **type-only** imports and re-exports
     (`import type`, `export type`, `import { type X }`), which are elided at
     compile time and cannot evaluate Phaser;
   - treats a resolved `phaser` specifier reached through a **value** edge as a
     violation, and reports the full offending chain
     (`src/ui/X.ts → src/ui/Y.ts → phaser`);
   - exits `0` when every listed module is clean, non-zero with one line per
     violation (module, chain) otherwise; supports `--json` for tests;
   - is a total function over inputs: an unresolvable specifier inside
     `src/ui`/aliases is itself a violation (never a silent skip), and a listed
     module that does not exist is a violation.
   Wire it as `npm run check:ui-node-surface` and include it in the
   pre-implementation gate used by `implement.py finish` / the dev-push path
   (resolved: Q2 → A, hard gate).
3. **Extend the guard test to the manifest.** `tests/ui/phaser-free-imports.test.ts`
   keeps its throwing-mock + negative control, but iterates the manifest so
   adding an entry automatically gets an evaluation-based guard too — the two
   mechanisms are complementary (static graph check = complete coverage and
   order independence; throwing mock = proof that the runtime actually starts
   without Phaser).
4. **Docs + barrel comment.** `docs/DEVELOPER.md` § *Phaser-free `@ui` helper
   imports for Node tests* gains the manifest as the authoritative list (link +
   the "adding a module" procedure), states the check and its npm script, and
   replaces "when in doubt, probe with `vite-node`" with "look it up in the
   manifest; if it is not listed, treat it as Phaser-bearing". `src/ui/index.ts`
   gains a short docblock above `UI_VERSION` stating explicitly that the barrel
   is **intentionally** Phaser-bearing (`CardGameScene extends Phaser.Scene`),
   that Node tests must import deep Phaser-free paths, and pointing at the
   manifest + check. `docs/ui-animations.md` node-safe note gains the same
   pointer.

Non-goals: no change to any runtime behaviour, public signature, barrel export
list, or `src/ui/constants.ts` value; no attempt to make the whole of `src/ui`
node-safe; no sibling-repo edits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/ui/node-safe-modules.ts` exists, is Phaser-free and side-effect-free,
      and exports a typed readonly manifest of node-safe `src/ui` module paths
      with a one-line rationale per entry; every listed entry was verified by
      the new check (not assumed from a regex probe).
- [ ] `scripts/check-ui-node-surface.ts` walks the real import graph for every
      manifest entry (following the `tsconfig.json` path aliases), ignores
      type-only edges, and exits non-zero naming the module and the offending
      chain when a listed module transitively has a **value** import of
      `phaser` or of a Phaser-bearing module such as `src/ui/Renderer`.
- [ ] The check is **proved to have teeth**: unit tests in
      `tests/scripts/check-ui-node-surface.test.ts` cover (a) a clean manifest
      exiting 0, (b) a value `import Phaser from 'phaser'` entry failing with the
      offending path in the output, (c) a transitive failure through an alias
      (`@core-engine/*` or `@ui/*`), (d) a **type-only** Phaser import passing,
      (e) an unresolvable specifier failing closed, (f) a missing listed module
      failing, and (g) the real repo manifest passing (a live regression gate).
- [ ] `tests/ui/phaser-free-imports.test.ts` iterates the manifest so every
      listed module is imported at runtime under the throwing `phaser` mock,
      keeping its negative control (`@ui/Renderer` fails, mock call count
      increases) so the guard cannot silently pass.
- [ ] `npm run check:ui-node-surface` is wired into the implementation gate
      (per Q2) and runs green on a clean tree; a deliberately introduced Phaser
      value import in a listed module makes it fail (documented in the item
      comment with the command output).
- [ ] `docs/DEVELOPER.md` documents the manifest as the authoritative node-safe
      list, the check + npm script, and the "adding a module to the surface"
      procedure, and retires the "probe with `vite-node` when in doubt" advice in
      favour of the lookup; `src/ui/index.ts` carries a docblock stating the
      barrel is intentionally Phaser-bearing and that Node tests must import
      deep Phaser-free paths; `docs/ui-animations.md` links the manifest.
      Code comments cross-link `CG-0MVS9HBN3009HIQN`.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] `npm run build` (TypeScript strict + Vite) succeeds.

## Constraints

- **No new dependencies:** the check uses the TypeScript compiler API
  (`typescript`, already a devDependency). Do not add an AST/lexer package.
- **Core-only:** no edits to sibling `tce-<game>` repos. Sibling findings are
  read-only evidence and, at most, a note in this item.
- **No behaviour change:** nothing in `src/ui` runtime code changes except the
  `index.ts` docblock. If a candidate manifest entry turns out to be
  Phaser-bearing, **drop it from the manifest** rather than editing that module
  to accommodate the list (changing a module's import graph is a separate item).
- **Type-only Phaser references stay legal** and must keep compiling under
  `isolatedModules` (`import type`).
- **The check must be deterministic and fast** (seconds, no bundler, no Vitest
  run, no network) so it can run on every push.
- **Fail closed:** an unresolvable specifier, a missing listed module, or a
  manifest file that cannot be parsed is a failure — never a warning.
- **Do not restructure the `@ui` barrel** or remove existing exports; scenes
  consume them today.
- Unit tests are the minimum gate during implementation; the full suite is
  required before the `dev` push.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/node-safe-modules.ts` — NEW: the typed readonly manifest (~15 entries) + one-line rationale per entry; plain data, no imports.
- `scripts/check-ui-node-surface.ts` — NEW: TypeScript-compiler-API import-graph check over the manifest; alias-aware, type-only-eliding, fail-closed, `--json` output.
- `tests/scripts/check-ui-node-surface.test.ts` — NEW: teeth tests (clean / direct value import / transitive via alias / type-only OK / unresolvable / missing module / real-repo manifest).
- `tests/ui/phaser-free-imports.test.ts` — Iterate the manifest instead of a hard-coded four-entry list; keep the throwing mock, the `phaserMock.calls === 0` assertion, and the `@ui/Renderer` negative control.
- `package.json` — NEW script `check:ui-node-surface`; wire into the gate chosen in Q2.
- `src/ui/index.ts` — Docblock above `UI_VERSION`: barrel is intentionally Phaser-bearing, Node tests import deep Phaser-free paths, link the manifest + check.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — § *Phaser-free `@ui` helper imports for Node tests*: manifest as the authoritative list, check + script, "adding a module" procedure, retire the probe-when-in-doubt advice.
- `docs/ui-animations.md` — Node-safe note under the `shakeIllegalMove` import block: point at the manifest.
- `AGENTS.md` — Only if the new npm script / gate changes developer workflow (Doc-Update Policy); otherwise no change.

## Risks and assumptions

- **False promise risk (medium):** listing a module as node-safe when it is not.
  Mitigation: every entry is verified by the new check during implementation;
  candidates that fail are dropped rather than patched.
- **Regex-probe trust risk (addressed):** the intake probe ignored path aliases,
  so the "44 Phaser-free" figure may be too high. Mitigation: the manifest starts
  deliberately narrow (the modules downstream node tests actually import plus the
  already-documented four) and grows only through verification.
- **Alias-resolution drift (medium):** the check must resolve aliases exactly as
  `vite.config.ts`/`tsconfig.json` do, or it will silently skip
  `@core-engine/*` edges. Mitigation: read `paths` from `tsconfig.json` (single
  source) and add the transitive-via-alias test case (AC 3c).
- **Maintenance burden (low–medium):** a listed module's author now has an extra
  constraint. Mitigation: narrow opt-in list + a failure message that names the
  module and chain, plus the "adding a module" procedure in the docs.
- **Check duplicating the guard (low):** two mechanisms could drift.
  Mitigation: both consume the same manifest, so they cannot disagree about
  *which* modules are promised.
- **Gate friction risk (medium):** adding a check to `implement.py finish` /
  pre-push could slow or block unrelated work if it is flaky. Mitigation: it is
  pure static analysis with no bundler/network, and Q2 asks the producer to
  choose whether it is a hard gate or a test-only check.
- **Scope-creep risk:** making all of `src/ui` node-safe, extracting a shared
  Phaser-free style builder (noted in `CG-0MVQQ2M8E003FQMZ`), or refactoring the
  barrel are **out of scope**; record them as separate items if they prove
  worthwhile.
- **Assumption:** the throwing-`phaser`-mock guard remains the runtime proof;
  this item only adds a *complete, order-independent* static complement, so the
  existing guard must not be weakened or removed.
- **Assumption:** no browser test asserts anything this item touches (docs and
  the barrel docblock only), so no browser suite change is expected.

## Resolved producer decisions

All three decisions were answered **A** (the recommended options), so the brief
above stands exactly as drafted; no AC changes were needed.

- **Q1 → A** — curated opt-in manifest (~15 entries; the modules downstream Node
  unit tests actually import, plus the four already documented). The check
  enforces the listed set; it is **not** a completeness snapshot of `src/ui`.
- **Q2 → A** — the static check is a **hard gate**: `npm run check:ui-node-surface`
  plus unit-test coverage, wired into the implementation / dev-push gate.
- **Q3 → A** — the manifest lives in `src/ui/node-safe-modules.ts` as a typed
  `as const` list with a one-line rationale per entry, consumed by both the
  check script and `tests/ui/phaser-free-imports.test.ts`.

Confirmation status: **ready to plan** — no open questions remain.

## Related work

- **CG-0MVQQ2M8E003FQMZ** — "[test-failure] @ui barrel statically imports
  Phaser — downstream game unit suites fail with 'window is not defined'"
  (completed, shipped in v0.1.22): made `illegalMoveToastView` Phaser-free,
  added `tests/ui/phaser-free-imports.test.ts`, documented the rule in
  `docs/DEVELOPER.md` + `docs/ui-animations.md`, and **explicitly deferred**
  the documented surface + static import-graph check to this item.
- **CG-0MVPXFHBZ004LGEB** — "Core illegal-move routine: explain a rejected move
  with a reason toast" (completed): the change that introduced the regression,
  now fixed.
- **CG-0MSXKQVZC009AM9L** — "Play illegal move audio/visual when hand is full
  during buy" (completed): earlier consumer of the same shake/toast helper graph.
- **MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG** — `tce-main-street` Bank Loans epic: was blocked by
  the regression; the sibling pin bump is tracked there, not here.
- Duplicate check performed (`wl search`: *phaser*, *node-safe*, *import guard*,
  *window is not defined*, *ui barrel*) — no item satisfies these ACs; the
  predecessor is the cause and defers option C here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — Scope of the documented node-safe surface.** Options: (A) curated
  opt-in list of the `src/ui` modules that downstream Node unit tests actually
  import, plus the four already documented; (B) every `src/ui` module that is
  currently Phaser-free (approximate regex probe: 44 of 62 top-level modules),
  maintained as a snapshot; (C) prose list in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` only, no
  machine-readable manifest. **Recommended:** A — a narrow promise is cheap to
  keep and covers the real consumer set; B promises node-safety for
  scene-coupled modules (`PileView`, `Overlay`, `HandView`, …) that nobody
  imports in Node, and C is what already exists and is not enforced.
  **Answer (producer):** **A** — curated opt-in list. Source: producer reply in this
  session ("1. A"). Effect: the manifest is scoped to the ~15 entries the
  downstream Node unit tests actually import plus the four already documented;
  the check enforces only the listed set (no completeness snapshot).
  Source: this intake session (auto-dispatched; no operator present). Effect
  once answered: A narrows the manifest to ~15 entries, B expands it to ~44 and
  makes the check a completeness snapshot, C removes the manifest and the
  manifest-driven guard extension.
- **Q2 — Enforcement of the static import-graph check.** Options: (A) hard gate:
  `npm run check:ui-node-surface` runs in the implementation/dev-push gate and
  the unit tests cover it; (B) test-only: the check is exercised only by
  `tests/scripts/check-ui-node-surface.test.ts` plus one real-repo assertion, no
  npm-script gate; (C) defer the check entirely, ship the manifest + docs now.
  **Recommended:** A — the whole point of the follow-up is catching the
  regression *before* downstream suites do, and the check is pure static
  analysis (no bundler, no network, seconds).
  **Answer (producer):** **A** — hard gate. Source: producer reply in this session
  ("2. A"). Effect: `npm run check:ui-node-surface` is added and wired into the
  implementation / dev-push gate, and `tests/scripts/check-ui-node-surface.test.ts`
  covers it as written in AC 3.
  Source: this intake session. Effect: A adds a `package.json` script plus gate
  wiring, B leaves the check test-covered only, C drops `scripts/` and
  `tests/scripts/check-ui-node-surface.test.ts` from scope.
- **Q3 — Manifest location and format.** Options: (A) `src/ui/node-safe-modules.ts`
  (typed `as const` list + rationale comments); (B) `src/ui/node-safe-modules.json`
  (data file); (C) a comment block in `src/ui/index.ts` only. **Recommended:** A
  — type-checked, importable by both the check and the guard test, and it keeps
  the rationale next to the entry. B splits prose from data; C cannot be consumed
  programmatically, so the check would need a second copy of the list.
  **Answer (producer):** **A** — typed TS module. Source: producer reply in this
  session ("3. A"). Effect: the manifest lives in `src/ui/node-safe-modules.ts`
  (typed `as const` list with per-entry rationale), consumed by both the check
  and the guard test; ACs 1–4 stand as written.
  Source: this intake session. Effect: A is implemented by ACs 1–4 as written;
  B changes the manifest file type and the loader; C degrades ACs 1, 3 and 4
  (no manifest to iterate) and reduces the check to a hard-coded list.
- **Q4 (informational, no producer input needed) — Duplicate check.** Searched
  *phaser*, *node-safe*, *import guard*, *window is not defined*, *ui barrel*.
  Result: `CG-0MVQQ2M8E003FQMZ` (the fix, which defers option C here) and
  `CG-0MVPXFHBZ004LGEB` (the toast feature). No covering item — no duplicate.
  Source: `wl search` runs in this intake session.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MVQQ2M8E003FQMZ** – [test-failure] @ui barrel statically imports Phaser — downstream game unit suites fail with 'window is not defined' (completed)
- **CG-0MVPXFHBZ004LGEB** – Core illegal-move routine: explain a rejected move with a reason toast (completed)
- **CG-0MSXKQVZC009AM9L** – Play illegal move audio/visual when hand is full during buy (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: barrel, bearing, cardgamescene, deep,
  documented, dragdrop, downstream, entry, environment, evaluation, graph,
  guard, helpers, illegalmovetoastview, import, node, phaser, renderer, safe,
  shakeillegalmove, static, unit, value (+52 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: barrel, cardgamescene, deep, documented, graph, guard,

data.description:
# Typed node-safe module manifest for `src/ui`

**Goal:** A single source of truth — a typed, machine-readable manifest of the
`src/ui` modules that are guaranteed importable in a plain Node environment (no
`window`, no Phaser evaluation), so downstream `tce-<game>` unit suites and
engine maintainers can *look up* node-safety instead of probing. Parent:
CG-0MVS9HBN3009HIQN.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/ui/node-safe-modules.ts` exists and exports a readonly `as const`
      array (`uiNodeSafeModules`) of `src/ui` module paths; the file is itself
      Phaser-free and side-effect-free (a plain data module — no value imports,
      no module-scope side effects) so the check, the guard test and docs
      tooling can all import it.
- [ ] Every entry carries a one-line rationale comment (what it is / why it must
      stay framework-free).
- [ ] The initial list is the 15 intake candidates (`illegalMoveToast`,
      `illegalMoveToastView`, `shakeIllegalMove`, `dragDrop`, `screen-layout`,
      `screen-layout-compose`, `screen-layout-schema`, `constants`,
      `SettingsStore`, `card-pack-url`, `card-pack-client`, `game-asset-url`,
      `game-manifest`, `game-plugin-boot`, `content-unlock-client`); each entry
      is verified by the new static check during implementation, and any that
      prove Phaser-bearing is **dropped, not patched**.
- [ ] `tests/ui/node-safe-modules.test.ts` (or equivalent unit) asserts: entries
      are unique, non-empty strings with no duplicates; each entry maps to an
      existing `src/ui/<entry>.ts`; the manifest array type is readonly.
- [ ] Code comments cross-link CG-0MVS9HBN3009HIQN.


- [ ] `src/ui/node-safe-modules.ts` exists, is Phaser-free and side-effect-free,
      and exports a typed readonly manifest of node-safe `src/ui` module paths
      with a one-line rationale per entry; every listed entry was verified by
      the new check (not assumed from a regex probe).

## Minimal implementation

# Static import-graph check (TypeScript compiler API)

**Goal:** `scripts/check-ui-node-surface.ts` — a deterministic, seconds-fast,
compiler-based static check that walks the real import graph for every manifest
entry and fails when a listed module transitively reaches a Phaser **value**
import, so a reintroduced regression is caught here, not in 23 downstream game
suites with `window is not defined`. Parent: CG-0MVS9HBN3009HIQN.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] For every entry in the manifest, resolves and walks the module graph using
      the **same `paths`/aliases as `tsconfig.json`** (all of
      `@core-engine/*`, `@card-system/*`, `@rule-engine/*`, `@ai/*`, `@ui/*`
      are followed, not skipped).
- [ ] Ignores **type-only** imports and re-exports (`import type`,
      `export type`, `import { type X }`) — elided at compile time — while a
      resolved `phaser` specifier reached through a **value** edge is a
      violation reported with the full offending chain
      (`src/ui/X.ts → src/ui/Y.ts → phaser`).
- [ ] **Fail closed:** an unresolvable specifier inside `src/ui`/an alias, a
      listed module that does not exist, and an unparseable manifest file are
      each a violation (never a warning, never a silent skip).
- [ ] CLI contract: exits `0` when every listed module is clean; non-zero with
      one line per violation (module, chain); supports `--json` for tests;
      supports `--manifest <path>` / `--root <dir>` overrides for hermetic
      fixture tests.
- [ ] The real repo manifest passes (green); all cases in the teeth-test item
      pass. Uses only the TypeScript compiler API (`typescript` devDependency —
      **no new dependency**).
- [ ] Code comments cross-link CG-0MVS9HBN3009HIQN.


- [ ] `scripts/check-ui-node-surface.ts` walks the real import graph for every
      manifest entry (following the `tsconfig.json` path aliases), ignores
      type-only edges, and exits non-zero naming the module and the offending
      chain when a listed module transitively has a **value** import of
      `phaser` or of a Phaser-bearing module such as `src/ui/Renderer`.

## Minimal implementation

- Implement the compiler-API walker (resolve module specs via `tsconfig.json`
  `paths`; follow local + alias value edges; reject on `phaser` value edges).
- Add the CLI entry (`#!/usr/bin/env node`, argument parsing, exit codes).
- Run against the real manifest; iterate the teeth tests to green.

## Key files

- `scripts/check-ui-node-surface.ts` — NEW: the check.

## Dependencies

- Edge to the manifest item (consumes `uiNodeSafeModules`).
- Edge to the teeth-tests item (its passing tests are the contract).
